summary.text: Mollusca is a phylum of invertebrate animals with 89,857 recognised living species, making it the second-largest animal phylum.
Four features define modern molluscs: a soft body of almost all muscle, a mantle with a cavity for breathing and excretion, a radula except in bivalves, and the structure of the nervous system.
They are the largest marine phylum, and include snails and slugs as well as squid, cuttlefish and octopuses.

facts.label: Largest invertebrate
facts.value: The giant or the colossal squid

items.prompt: A garden snail scrapes its food with a rasping, tongue-like organ. What is that organ called?

options.label: The mantle
The radula
The foot
The cilia

items.explain: The generalized mollusc feeds with a rasping tongue called the radula, which most molluscs have except bivalves.

items.prompt: On the hypothetical ancestral mollusc, one limpet-like shell sits on top. What produces that shell?

options.label: The muscular foot on the underside
The rasping tongue used for feeding
The cilia that move food through the gut
The mantle covering the whole upper surface

items.explain: The single shell is secreted by a mantle covering the whole upper surface. The foot is a muscular structure on the underside.

items.prompt: A biologist watches a mollusc egg hatch and finds a tiny copy of the adult instead of a larva. Is that possible?

options.label: Yes, since some molluscs hatch as miniature adults, while others emerge as larvae
No, since every mollusc hatches as a larva and changes later
No, since molluscs give birth to live young rather than eggs
Yes, but only in the groups that have a shell

items.explain: Nearly all molluscs produce eggs, from which may emerge trochophore larvae, more complex veliger larvae, or miniature adults.

items.prompt: A tropical cone shell can kill with a sting. Why do researchers still value it?

options.label: Its venom is used to cure food poisoning from other molluscs
Its shell was once used as money in some preindustrial societies
Its venoms are sophisticated yet easy to make, so they aid neurological research
It is a source of pearls, mother of pearl and a purple dye

items.explain: Stings from large cone shells can kill, but their venoms have become important tools in neurological research.

items.prompt: Why do many places have rules about molluscs that are sold as food?

options.label: Molluscs are the largest marine phylum and are quickly overfished
Toxins can build up in certain molluscs and cause food poisoning
Their venom bites could be fatal to the people eating them
Their shells are valuable and can be sold as luxury goods

items.explain: Molluscs are an important food source, but toxins can accumulate in some under specific conditions, so many jurisdictions regulate to reduce the risk.

items.prompt: Imagine drawing one classified mollusc species at random. Which class would you most likely draw?

options.label: Gastropods, the snails, slugs and abalone
Cephalopods, such as squid and octopuses
Bivalves, which lack a radula
One of the classes that are entirely extinct

items.explain: Gastropods are by far the most diverse class and account for 80% of classified molluscan species.
